deferredForEditableCoding.completeSourceBrief: | `BD-V-037` | Pablo; User | Essential | Diagram | 27 | Pablo: add a public/private-key image and optional physical teaching tool. User: place a public/private-key relationship diagram after this section with an explicit warning never to share a private key. | SG: At the end of `### Keys` in the [Student Guide](../publish/mfb-bd-26.10/mfb-bd-sg-26.10.md#keys), after the `Try it` sorting prompt and immediately before `### Seed phrases`. EG: under `### Keys and digital authorization`, replace the matching marker after the source text at the listed EG line. See section 3.8 for the exact anchor. | SG: 844; EG: 1954 | Reinforces the rule “Public receiving information can be shared. Private spending information must remain secret” by showing how public information relates to a secret private key. | Show `Private key → Public key → Receiving address`, with the first arrow labelled `Derived from` and the address step labelled `Created from public-key information`. Place the private key inside a clearly marked secret boundary. Add a prominent warning beside it: `Never share your private key. Anyone with it can spend your bitcoin.` Use a warning symbol and readable text so the warning works in grayscale. Label the receiving address `Public receiving information`. Add a small signing branch: the private key creates a digital signature; nodes use the public key to verify it without seeing the private key. Keep the private key inside the secret boundary throughout. Do not imply that a public key or address can reveal the private key, that an address and public key are identical, or that a signature contains the private key. Use conceptual symbols only, never real or realistic private-key strings, recovery phrases, or scannable secrets. Caption: `Public information supports receiving and verification. The private key authorizes spending and must stay secret.` Alt text: `A private key kept inside a secret boundary derives a public key, from which receiving-address information is created. A separate branch shows signing and public verification without revealing the private key. Warning: never share your private key; anyone with it can spend your bitcoin.` Save the editable master as `y_assets (archived)/diploma/bd-v-037.svg`. | One-way key-relationship diagram with a prominent private-key warning and a supporting signing branch; full width. |
